meta.title: Operation of Vacuum Desiccator in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To store hygroscopic crude drug powders, phytochemical isolates, and dried extracts under vacuum in the presence of a desiccant to prevent moisture re-absorption and maintain sample integrity.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for post-drying storage of moisture-sensitive samples and cooling hot samples to room temperature without moisture uptake prior to weighing.
procedure: Inspect the vacuum desiccator for cracks in the glass dome, chip or damage on the ground glass rim, and integrity of the stopcock.
Renew the desiccant in the base compartment if it has changed colour (silica gel changes from blue to pink when saturated).
Apply a thin, uniform layer of high-vacuum grease (silicone or Apiezon) to the ground glass rim to ensure an airtight seal.
Place the porcelain plate inside the desiccator body above the desiccant.
Place the dried or hot samples in open containers (watch glasses, Petri dishes, weighing boats) on the porcelain plate — do not stack samples.
Place the glass dome on the ground glass rim and rotate slightly to distribute the grease evenly and ensure an airtight seal.
Connect the vacuum pump to the desiccator outlet with a vacuum tubing.
Switch on the vacuum pump and slowly open the stopcock — draw vacuum gradually to avoid disturbing sample.
Monitor the vacuum gauge — typically maintain 20–50 mbar vacuum.
Once the required vacuum is achieved, close the stopcock and switch off the vacuum pump.
Store the desiccator in a secure position on a flat surface — do not move while under vacuum.
To remove samples: slowly open the stopcock to bleed air in gradually — rapid air entry can disturb fine powders.
Once pressure equalizes, lift the dome carefully.
Remove samples promptly and weigh immediately to minimize moisture re-absorption.
Log sample name, date stored, vacuum level, and desiccant condition in the register.
precautions: Handle glass vacuum desiccators with great care — they are under external atmospheric pressure when evacuated and implode if cracked.
Never place desiccators on the edge of a bench — a fall under vacuum is an implosion hazard.
Bleed air back slowly — rapid air entry scatters fine powders and can crack hot glass vessels.
Renew desiccant regularly — saturated desiccant provides no moisture protection.
Do not apply excessive vacuum grease — excess grease contaminates samples.
For large desiccators, wrap the glass dome with a towel during evacuation as added implosion protection.
Check the stopcock for smooth operation and absence of leaks before each use.
Do not evacuate when the dome shows any cracks, chips, or opacification.
